topic: Binance $6.3B hack — 29 October 2026, largest crypto theft on record
fact_check_rule: Every `claim` below is backed by an `exact_source_sentence` copied verbatim from the linked article. Nothing is inferred beyond what the sentence states.

facts.claim: On 29 October 2026 an attacker moved about USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets across ten blockchains, most of it within about 20 minutes starting at 20:05 UTC.
facts.exact_source_sentence: On October 29, 2026, an attacker moved approximately USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes starting at 20:05 UTC.

facts.claim: Chainalysis independently estimated the unauthorised transfers at roughly $6.4 billion and called it the largest theft in crypto history.
facts.exact_source_sentence: Around 4:20 p.m. ET on October 29, 2026, funds began leaving Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains. Unauthorized transfers totaled approximately $6.4 billion, the largest theft in crypto history.

facts.claim: The theft was roughly four times the previous record, the $1.5 billion Bybit hack of February 2025.
facts.exact_source_sentence: That makes this the largest crypto theft on record, about four times the USD 1.5 billion Bybit hack of February 2025.

facts.claim: A single Bitcoin hot wallet sent 18,270 BTC to the attacker; Bitcoin has no issuer that can freeze it.
facts.exact_source_sentence: At 20:20 UTC, a Binance Bitcoin hot wallet sent 18,270 BTC to an attacker address, which began splitting the funds into round 1,000 BTC and 100 BTC pieces inside the same block.

facts.claim: About $3 billion of the stolen funds was frozen by stablecoin issuers and partners, but roughly $2.4 billion had already moved beyond any issuer's reach.
facts.exact_source_sentence: But the hackers have already moved $2.4 billion in crypto "beyond any issuer's reach," according to TRM.

facts.claim: Tether and Circle froze more than $2.3 billion of the stolen stablecoins.
facts.exact_source_sentence: Binance said about $3bn of that has since been frozen, including more than $2.3bn by stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle, according to the Reuters news agency.

facts.claim: Binance reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the stolen assets and promised users would not bear the loss.
facts.exact_source_sentence: The company said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the stolen assets and was beginning to recover assets for users.

facts.claim: The initial foothold came from a fake job interview: a software engineer downloaded a malicious code repository onto his computer after interviewing for a role at a fictitious company, including meeting its 'CEO' virtually.
facts.exact_source_sentence: Then in September a second software engineer seeking a new job downloaded "malicious code repository" onto ‌his computer after interviewing for what the person thought was a legitimate role, including meeting virtually with the CEO of a fictitious company.

facts.claim: Months earlier, in June 2026, a Wallet DevOps employee downloaded a fake Homebrew installer while trying to install an AI coding tool.
facts.exact_source_sentence: According to Binance's investigation, in June 2026, a Wallet DevOps employee downloaded a fake Homebrew installer while trying to install an AI coding tool.

facts.claim: On 29 October the attacker used the compromised wallet developer computers plus stolen credentials to trigger a malicious script that launched the theft.
facts.exact_source_sentence: On Oct. 29 the attacker used the second wallet developer's computer, using stolen credentials from the first wallet developer, and triggered a malicious script to launch the attack.

facts.claim: The FBI attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, North Korean state-sponsored cyber actors.
facts.exact_source_sentence: The Federal Bureau of Investigation on Saturday reported that TraderTraitor — cyber actors sponsored by North Korea since at least 2020 — were responsible for the theft.

facts.claim: Binance resumed withdrawals in phases on 1 November 2026, absorbing the financial impact itself rather than passing it to users.
facts.exact_source_sentence: “Today, we're beginning the phased resumption of withdrawals, taking a careful approach to ensure services return safely and securely,” Binance co-CEO Richard Teng posted on X early Sunday. “Our commitment remains clear: Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users.”

facts.claim: Binance's emergency SAFU reserve held about $1 billion, only a fraction of the amount impacted.
facts.exact_source_sentence: Held entirely in Bitcoin, SAFU's assets were valued at $1 billion earlier this month — a sixth of the amount impacted by Thursday's hack.

facts.claim: The attacker had prepared 50 pre-signed authorisations in advance, submitted in a single transaction, to turn a Binance hot wallet into a sweeper contract it controlled.
facts.exact_source_sentence: At 20:20 UTC, the operator submitted a single transaction containing 50 authorizations. Each was signed by the Binance hot wallet, and each pointed it to a sweeper contract that accepts instructions only from the operator.
